## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Giridattajātaka* (Ja 184) is a Jātaka tale translated as *The Groom Giridatta*. According to the narrative framework recorded in the text, the Buddha delivered the story while dwelling at Veḷuvana Park on the topic of keeping bad company, following background circumstances previously recounted in the *Mahilāmukhajātaka*. Addressing a monk who was keeping bad company, the Buddha noted that this monk had behaved identically in a former life before recounting the story of the past. In the index to the Jātaka collection compiled by V. Fausböll, the central character Giridatta (with the variants Giridanta and Giridattha) is identified as an *assabandha* (horse trainer or groom) in royal service [Fausböll 1897].
